components.name: Academische vaardigheden 1
components.note: Required academic writing and research skills, including a separately registered information-literacy practical and its test; attendance is required.

components.name: Motorische en perceptuele ontwikkeling
components.note: Studies motor and perceptual development in children. General neural perception and action are related background, not the same developmental course.

components.name: Beroepsvaardigheden 1
components.note: Required professional skills. This and Kennis in praktijk 1 have integrated assignments and must be taken together.

components.name: Kennis in praktijk 1
components.note: Required practice and reflection, coordinated with first-year professional skills. A UCR school rhetoric project offers a narrower experience.

components.name: Psychometrie en besliskunde
components.note: Psychometric instrument construction, reliability, validity and clinical decision-making; general statistics alone does not replace it.

components.name: Beroepsvaardigheden 2
components.note: Required professional interview, observation, test, reporting and reflection skills; entry follows passed professional skills 1. Attendance and all assignments must be sufficient.

components.name: Analyse 3
components.note: Qualitative concepts, interviews, thematic analysis and reflective reconceptualisation. All three assessed assignments must be sufficient.

components.name: Academische vaardigheden 2
components.note: Required academic research skills, following passed academic skills 1. Includes group empirical research and an individual research report.

components.name: Methodiek van de diagnostiek
components.note: One of two second-year courses in the selected Orthopedagogiek specialisation. Other specialisations are alternatives, not additional requirements.

components.name: Behandelingsmethodiek
components.note: Required treatment methodology within the selected Orthopedagogiek specialisation.

components.name: Vrije keuzeruimte jaar 2
components.note: 8 EC genuine open choice, subject to university-level, overlap and approval rules. Listed programme electives and the movement minor are optional.

components.name: Analyse 4
components.note: Dynamic and person-specific analysis using time series, recurrence, state-space grids, complexity and networks. Meta-analysis is a different research method.

components.name: Kennis in praktijk 3
components.note: Required year-long practice and reflection. Special early-completion arrangements require advance planning; they are not assumed.

components.name: Beroepsvaardigheden 3 Orthopedagogiek
components.note: Selected 8 EC Orthopedagogiek professional-skills variant, following passed professional skills 2 and all first-year courses. Preregistration is required; at most two attempts. The other skills variant is an alternative.

components.name: Orthopedagogiek - interventies
components.note: Third 4 EC course completing the coherent 12 EC Orthopedagogiek specialisation. Full first year is required.

components.name: Vrije keuzeruimte jaar 3
components.note: 16 EC genuine open choice, with optional programme electives, minor or approved outside study. It is not a compulsory movement minor.

components.name: Bachelorscriptie
components.note: Required 10 EC individual thesis, with a genuine choice of argumentative or empirical/review method. Full first year and preregistration are required. Empirical research may be conducted jointly, but the written thesis is individual; two readers assess the work.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Academic source work, questions, writing and reflection provide a foundation; Radboud adds discipline-specific research and information-literacy requirements.
Social institutions, cultural contexts and inequalities provide relevant background, without a dedicated childhood sociology focus.
Research design, sampling, experiments, statistics and a group research project provide related empirical foundations.
Qualitative design, data collection, interpretation and a group project relate directly to interviews and thematic qualitative inquiry in the target.
Inferential and multivariate statistical models provide substantial quantitative inquiry; the target has its own sequence and assessment context.
Memory, attention, emotion and experimental brain research provide related cognitive-neuropsychological foundations, not specialist child assessment practice.
Psychopathology explicitly spans infancy through adulthood; there is a genuine childhood connection within broader clinical study.
Actual infant, child and adolescent social/emotional development is studied alongside adulthood and ageing; scope differs.
Actual work with primary-school children on speaking and debating provides a narrower school-linked practice experience; it is not the target’s pedagogical placement.

Actual youth resilience research and evidence-based materials for educators offer a related intervention perspective focused on radicalisation prevention; not the whole orthopedagogical intervention sequence.

Assessment and psychotherapy explicitly include infants, children and adolescents as well as adults. This offers substantive introductory assessment study, not professional orthopedagogical qualification.
Language acquisition, bilingualism, reading and dyslexia provide substantive developmental connections within a broader neuropsycholinguistics course.
Ethical reasoning and applied argument contribute a normative perspective; children’s-rights law and professional-care rules remain distinct.

notes.text: The UCR programme offers related developmental, language, psychological-assessment and youth-support study, with substantial research methods. Several courses also address adults. Radboud additionally requires dedicated pedagogy and orthopedagogy, supervised professional practice and a pedagogical-sciences thesis. General psychology, a school rhetoric project and optional research do not replace that sequence or confer a professional qualification.

audience.programmeDescription: Pedagogical Sciences at Radboud studies children’s and young people’s development, upbringing, education and support when development is difficult. It combines developmental research with pedagogy, specialist assessment and intervention, supervised practice and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programme connects developmental psychology, language acquisition, childhood mental health and assessment with youth research and a primary-school communication project. Research methods support these connections. Several courses also cover adults or biological foundations. Dedicated pedagogy, orthopedagogy, supervised professional practice and the required pedagogical thesis remain significant differences.

curriculum.limitation: The complete 180 EC framework has 60 EC in each year. It includes 136 EC of common requirements, including a 10 EC thesis with a choice of method; 20 EC of coherent specialisation and professional-skills choices; and 24 EC of open choice. Orthopedagogiek is the first-listed specialisation; other branches are alternatives. The Dutch academic-language test is compulsory and adds no credits. Full first-year completion is required before year three; first-year progression normally requires 42 EC. UCR’s school rhetoric project uses principally Dutch interaction, so students should check language arrangements.
